resources.string: This note shows what to tap. It is an ordinary note, kept with your others: delete it when you are done.
Tap TODO to mark this done
The menu lists the note's keywords. The one you pick is written in the file, as Emacs would write it.
Tap this heading to edit it
Or tap this text: a heading and its text open together. Save and Discard are at the end of the strip above the keyboard. While editing, type [[ to link to a note, or < for a date.
Its menu adds a heading below or a sub-heading, moves this one, clocks in, sets a priority, or refiles it under another heading.
See the count in the heading change
Tap the date above: the calendar opens on that day, with this heading in it. Tap it there to come back; hold it to reschedule it or mark it done.
It opens as a grid, a field per cell. Change a number, then press Recalculate: the total is a #+TBLFM formula, computed as in Emacs.
The chevron beside a heading folds everything under it.
Hidden while the heading above is folded
%1$s takes you to the table; the back arrow at the top brings you here again. %2$s opens in the browser.
The ☰ button at the top lists your notes. Hold one to pin, rename or delete it.
Search finds words anywhere in your notes. Try tag:work, todo:TODO or priority:A.
The calendar shows your dates by day, by week or by month.
On a phone, share a link or some text from another app to KorgNote to keep it in a note.
Settings has reminders, where new notes go, and this tour again.
KorgNote can add a short note, Welcome to KorgNote, whose headings show what to tap: a TODO, a checkbox, a date, a table.
It is an ordinary note, saved with your others. Delete it once you are done.
